name: Testicular Germ Cell Tumors, Serum Markers, and Inguinal Orchiectomy

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / Campbell-Walsh Urology 12th ed
clinicalPearls: Testicular cancer represents the most common solid tumor in young men aged 15 to 35 years
Radical inguinal orchiectomy with high cord ligation is mandatory; transscrotal biopsy is strictly contraindicated
Pure seminomas never produce alpha-fetoprotein (AFP); elevated AFP indicates non-seminomatous elements
Cryptorchidism increases testicular malignancy risk in both the undescended and contralateral descended testicle
Retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (RPLND) is indicated for post-chemotherapy residual NSGCT masses > 1 cm
reference.pathophysiology: Germ cell tumors originate from germ cell neoplasia in situ (GCNIS) following primordial germ cell developmental arrest, typically bearing isochromosome 12p (i12p). Seminomas maintain primordial germ cell markers (OCT3/4, NANOG, PLAP), while non-seminomas differentiate into embryonal carcinoma (totipotent), yolk sac elements (AFP production), or choriocarcinoma (hCG production).
additionalInvestigations: Serum tumor markers: Alpha-fetoprotein, beta-hCG, and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH)
Contrast-enhanced computed tomography of chest, abdomen, and pelvis
Histopathological examination of inguinal orchiectomy specimen
